title: Biodiversity of Animals
seo_title: Grade 11 Life Sciences: Biodiversity of Animals Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 11 Life Sciences: Biodiversity of animals
standard_text: Classification of animals into phyla using body plans: symmetry, number of germ layers, body cavities (coelom), and the gut (one or two openings); the main phyla (Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Chordata); the role of invertebrates in ecosystems. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 11, Life Sciences: Biodiversity of animals)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): body plans, symmetry, germ layers, coeloms, the gut and the main animal phyla. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Animals are classified by their body plan.
key_sub: Arthropods have jointed legs and an exoskeleton.
body_html:
How to think about it

Body plans differ in symmetry (none, radial or bilateral), the number of germ layers (two or three), whether there is a body cavity (coelom), and whether the gut has one opening or two (mouth and anus).

Porifera (sponges) have no symmetry; Cnidaria (jellyfish) have radial symmetry and two germ layers; Platyhelminthes (flatworms) have three germ layers but no coelom; Annelida (earthworms) are segmented with a coelom; Arthropoda have jointed legs and an exoskeleton; Chordata have a notochord.

Example

Which phylum does a jellyfish belong to?

Radial symmetry, stinging cells

Answer: Cnidaria

Example

Which phylum has jointed legs?

Insects, spiders and crabs

Answer: Arthropoda

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all invertebrates are insects.
  • Mixing up radial and bilateral symmetry.
  • Thinking a spider is an insect.

faq.q: Why is a through-gut (two openings) an advantage?
faq.a: Food moves one way, so different parts can digest and absorb food at the same time.
They mix and aerate the soil and help decompose dead material.

items.q: What is a coelom?
c: a fluid-filled body cavity inside the mesoderm
the hole that forms the mouth
items.e: The coelom gives room for organs to develop and move.

items.q: Which phylum is triploblastic but has no coelom (acoelomate)?
items.e: Flatworms have solid bodies without a cavity.

items.q: Why is bilateral symmetry linked to cephalisation?
c: it lets animals stay attached to rocks
it means there is no brain
animals moving forward have a head end where sense organs and nerve cells collect
items.e: Cephalisation is the development of a head.

items.q: What is the advantage of a through-gut (mouth and anus)?
c: food moves in one direction, so digestion and absorption can happen at the same time in different parts
it makes the animal radially symmetrical
food can leave through the mouth
items.e: A blind sac gut has only one opening.

items.q: What is bilateral symmetry?
c: the body can be cut into halves along many planes
the body can be divided into two mirror-image halves along one plane only
the body is round like a ball
items.e: Most animals, including humans, are bilaterally symmetrical.

items.q: Triploblastic animals have …
c: three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm
items.e: The mesoderm forms muscles and organs.

items.q: What is radial symmetry?
c: the body can be cut into two mirror halves along one plane only
the body has a head and a tail
the body can be cut into similar halves along many planes through the centre
items.e: Cnidaria such as jellyfish are radially symmetrical.

items.q: Which phylum shows the cellular level of organisation?
items.e: Porifera: the cellular level of organisation.

items.q: Which animals show radial symmetry as adults?
items.e: Echinoderm larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

items.q: Which class of vertebrates is cold-blooded and has a three-chambered heart, with moist skin?
items.e: Most reptiles also have three chambers, but dry scaly skin.

items.q: Which phylum shows metameric segmentation and nephridia?
items.e: Annelida: metameric segmentation and nephridia.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Hemichordata?
c: jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton
a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
items.e: Hemichordata: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus.

items.q: Which phylum shows flat bodies and flame cells?
items.e: Platyhelminthes: flat bodies and flame cells.

items.q: Which mammal lays eggs?
items.e: It is a monotreme.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Annelida?
c: a water vascular system and spiny skin
the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)
items.e: Annelida: metameric segmentation and nephridia.

items.q: What are cnidoblasts used for?
items.e: They contain stinging capsules.

items.q: What is the excretory organ of insects?
items.e: They remove waste into the gut.

items.q: Which is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom?
items.e: About two-thirds of all named species are arthropods.

items.q: Which phylum has a blind sac gut (one opening)?
items.e: Food enters and waste leaves through the same opening.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Ctenophora?
c: a water vascular system and spiny skin
a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton
items.e: Ctenophora: comb plates and bioluminescence.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Arthropoda?
items.e: A locust: Arthropoda.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Platyhelminthes?
items.e: A planarian: Platyhelminthes.

items.q: To which phylum does a bristleworm belong?
items.e: A bristleworm: Annelida.

items.q: To which phylum does a sea anemone belong?
items.e: A sea anemone: Cnidaria.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Chordata?
items.e: A sunbird: Chordata.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Porifera?
items.e: A sponge: Porifera.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Arthropoda?
items.e: A spider: Arthropoda.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Platyhelminthes?
items.e: A tapeworm: Platyhelminthes.

items.q: To which phylum does a bluebottle belong?
items.e: A bluebottle: Cnidaria.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Arthropoda?
items.e: A millipede: Arthropoda.

items.q: To which phylum does a scorpion belong?
items.e: A scorpion: Arthropoda.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Platyhelminthes?
items.e: A liver fluke: Platyhelminthes.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Chordata?
items.e: A human: Chordata.

items.q: To which phylum does a crab belong?
items.e: A crab: Arthropoda.

items.q: To which phylum does an earthworm belong?
items.e: An earthworm: Annelida.

items.q: To which phylum does a leech belong?
items.e: A leech: Annelida.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Cnidaria?
items.e: A coral polyp: Cnidaria.

items.q: To which phylum does a planarian belong?
items.e: A planarian: Platyhelminthes.

items.q: Which animal belongs to the phylum Cnidaria?
items.e: A jellyfish: Cnidaria.

items.q: To which phylum does a sponge belong?
items.e: A sponge: Porifera.

items.q: Why are coral reefs important?
c: they produce most of the world's fresh water
they support a very high biodiversity of marine life
items.e: Corals are Cnidaria that build limestone skeletons.

items.q: Which phylum has bilateral symmetry, three germ layers, a flat body and no coelom?
items.e: Platyhelminthes: bilateral symmetry, three germ layers, a flat body and no coelom.

items.q: Which phylum shows the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)?
items.e: Cnidaria: the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells).

items.q: Which feature describes the phylum Cnidaria?
c: no symmetry and no true tissues; the body has many pores
a notochord and a dorsal nerve cord at some stage of life
jointed legs and an exoskeleton made of chitin
radial symmetry, two germ layers and stinging cells
items.e: Cnidaria: radial symmetry, two germ layers and stinging cells.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Arthropoda?
c: jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton
a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)
items.e: Arthropoda: jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton.

items.q: Which phylum has a notochord and a dorsal nerve cord at some stage of life?
items.e: Chordata: a notochord and a dorsal nerve cord at some stage of life.

items.q: Why are insects successful on land?
c: they have an exoskeleton that prevents water loss and jointed legs for movement
items.e: The waterproof exoskeleton reduces drying out.

items.q: Which phylum includes the largest number of species?
items.e: Insects alone have over a million known species.

items.q: Which phylum shows jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton?
items.e: Arthropoda: jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton.

items.q: Which phylum has no symmetry and no true tissues; the body has many pores?
items.e: Porifera: no symmetry and no true tissues; the body has many pores.

items.q: Which chordates have a notochord only in the larval tail?
items.e: e.g. Ascidia and Salpa.

items.q: Which phylum has jointed legs and an exoskeleton made of chitin?
items.e: Arthropoda: jointed legs and an exoskeleton made of chitin.

items.q: Why is a flat body an advantage for a flatworm?
c: it gives a large surface area for gaseous exchange by diffusion
items.e: Flatworms have no lungs or gills.

items.q: Which phylum has radial symmetry, two germ layers and stinging cells?
items.e: Cnidaria: radial symmetry, two germ layers and stinging cells.

items.q: Which feature describes the phylum Arthropoda?
c: jointed legs and an exoskeleton made of chitin
a segmented body with a true coelom
bilateral symmetry, three germ layers, a flat body and no coelom
radial symmetry, two germ layers and stinging cells
items.e: Arthropoda: jointed legs and an exoskeleton made of chitin.

items.q: Which phylum has a segmented body with a true coelom?
items.e: Annelida: a segmented body with a true coelom.

items.q: How do earthworms help farmers?
c: they make burrows that aerate and drain the soil and they mix organic matter into it
items.e: Earthworms improve soil fertility.

items.q: Which feature describes the phylum Annelida?
c: no symmetry and no true tissues; the body has many pores
jointed legs and an exoskeleton made of chitin
radial symmetry, two germ layers and stinging cells
a segmented body with a true coelom
items.e: Annelida: a segmented body with a true coelom.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Cnidaria?
c: a water vascular system and spiny skin
the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)
items.e: Cnidaria: the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells).

items.q: Which feature describes the phylum Porifera?
c: a segmented body with a true coelom
no symmetry and no true tissues; the body has many pores
jointed legs and an exoskeleton made of chitin
a notochord and a dorsal nerve cord at some stage of life
items.e: Porifera: no symmetry and no true tissues; the body has many pores.

items.q: Which bacteria produce methane (biogas) in the guts of cows?
items.e: They are archaebacteria.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Plantae?
c: multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin
multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
items.e: Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food.

items.q: Which protists cause red tides?
items.e: They can release toxins that kill fish.

items.q: Which taxonomic aid is information about any one taxon?
items.e: monograph: information about any one taxon.

items.q: Why are fungi called saprophytes?
c: they absorb food from dead and decaying matter
items.e: They are important decomposers.

items.q: What is the cell wall of diatoms made of?
items.e: Their deposits form diatomaceous earth.

items.q: Which phylum shows a water vascular system and spiny skin?
items.e: Echinodermata: a water vascular system and spiny skin.

items.q: Which is the correct order from the highest to the lowest category?
c: species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
kingdom, class, phylum, order, family, genus, species
kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
kingdom, phylum, order, class, family, genus, species
items.e: Remember: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup.

items.q: Which kingdom has members that are multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food?
items.e: Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food.

items.q: Which is the basic unit of classification?
items.e: Members can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

items.q: Who discovered viruses?
items.e: From tobacco mosaic disease.

items.q: Which are the smallest living cells and have no cell wall?
items.e: They can survive without oxygen.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Animalia?
c: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: Which phylum shows a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle?
items.e: Mollusca: a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Mollusca?
c: jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton
the tissue level of organisation and cnidoblasts (stinging cells)
a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle
items.e: Mollusca: a soft body covered by a calcareous shell and a mantle.

items.q: What is the main drawback of the two-kingdom classification?
c: it puts prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular, together
items.e: Bacteria, fungi and plants were all in Plantae.

items.q: Which phylum shows a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus?
items.e: Hemichordata: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus.

items.q: Which category includes related genera?
items.e: e.g. Felidae includes Panthera and Felis.

items.q: What is a botanical garden?
c: a collection of preserved plant and animal specimens
a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study
a place where wild animals are kept in protected surroundings like their natural habitat
a book that helps identify the species in an area
items.e: botanical garden: a garden of living plants grown and labelled for study.

items.q: In Mangifera indica, what does 'indica' stand for?
items.e: Mangifera is the genus.

items.q: Which animals are diploblastic?
items.e: They have only ectoderm and endoderm.

items.q: Which feature is typical of phylum Porifera?
c: a stomochord and proboscis gland, as in Balanoglossus
items.e: Porifera: the cellular level of organisation.

items.q: Which animals have flame cells for excretion?
items.e: Flame cells also help in osmoregulation.

items.q: What are the three basic chordate features?
c: a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal gill slits
items.e: All appear at some stage of life.

items.q: Which phylum has a water vascular system for movement and feeding?
items.e: It moves by many small water-filled tubes (podia).

items.q: A disease kills most of the starfish on a rocky shore. What is the most likely result?
c: Urchins increase and kelp forests shrink.
Many new wetland species can live there.
Mussels take over and fewer species remain.
items.e: A keystone species has a large effect.

items.q: What is a pseudocoelomate?
c: an animal whose body cavity is not lined by mesoderm all round
an animal with no body cavity
an animal with a true coelom
items.e: e.g. roundworms (Aschelminthes).
